claims.text: First: pulse oximetry, ECG and CXR in most pts.
claims.quote: Most patients should initially have pulse oximetry, ECG, and chest radiographs.

claims.text: Troponin when Sx suggest ACS or ⍉other cause = clear; repeat troponin and ECG serially, since one norm set does ⍉r/o a ♡ cause.
claims.quote: Because a single normal set of cardiac biomarkers does not rule out a cardiac cause, patients whose symptoms suggest an acute coronary syndrome should have serial measurement of the cardiac biomarker troponin and serial ECGs.

claims.text: Cath w.in 90 minutes for ST elevation or high-risk NSTEMI.
claims.quote: Immediate catheterization is indicated in patients with ST-elevation on ECG or in patients with non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) plus high-risk features (eg, hypotension, ventricular arrhythmias, persistent chest pain despite optimal medical management), or high risk score (GRACE risk score [3]). In these patients, catheterization within 90 minutes of arrival is considered standard of care.

claims.text: POCUS or echocardiography in unstable pts, to look for ventricular dysfun, valve dz, effusion or tamponade.
claims.quote: Sometimes, particularly in patients with hemodynamic instability, either a point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) or a complete echocardiogram can also be useful in further evaluating potential life-threatening causes

claims.text: Abnorm aortic contour on CXR calls for testing for thoracic aortic dissection.
claims.quote: abnormal aortic contour on chest radiograph suggests need for testing for thoracic aortic dissection

claims.text: D-dimer for poss PE in low- or intermediate-risk pts.
claims.quote: If a pulmonary embolism (PE) is considered possible, D-dimer testing is done in patients who are at low or intermediate risk.
